title: Does Renters Insurance Cover Dog Bites? Coverage, Exclusions, and What Renters Should Check
summary: Usually yes — renters liability covers dog bites, at home or away. The catch: breed exclusions. What's covered, what isn't, and what to check first.
body_markdown:
## What's covered


Injuries to other people


Medical bills, lost wages, and legal liability when your dog bites a guest, a neighbor, or a stranger. Coverage follows the dog — the bite can happen at the dog park, on a walk, or in your apartment.


Your legal defense


If you're sued over a bite, the policy pays for your defense, separate from the liability limit itself.


Small bills, no fault needed


Medical-payments coverage (usually $1,000–$5,000) can pay a bitten guest's urgent-care bill without anyone proving fault — often enough to keep a small incident small.


Damage your dog does to others' property


If your dog destroys a neighbor's property, liability coverage generally applies the same way it would for an injury.


## What's not covered


Excluded breeds


Some carriers exclude breeds — commonly pit bulls, Rottweilers, and wolf hybrids — or any dog with a prior bite. Others, including some carriers we quote, evaluate by the individual dog's history instead. This is the single most important thing to check before you rely on the coverage.


Bites to your own household


If your dog bites you or someone who lives with you, liability coverage doesn't apply — that's what health insurance is for.


Your dog's own vet bills


Renters insurance never covers your pet's medical care. If your dog is injured — in a fight, an accident, or otherwise — that's a separate pet insurance policy.


Damage to your own apartment


Chewed carpet and scratched doors come out of your deposit. Policies exclude damage by your own pet to property in your care.


## Dogs and liability, in the leases we track


Most apartments welcome dogs — and the same leases that welcome them increasingly require liability coverage. Across the apartment communities in our dataset:


81%


of apartment communities with a stated pet policy allow dogs


$100,000


median liability coverage required by leases that mandate renters insurance


Source: SafeButler apartment dataset, 37,330 communities, July 2026. Dog acceptance based on 15,347 communities with an explicit species policy; liability figure from 255 leases specifying a required amount.


## Three things to check before you rely on it


First, breed language. Ask the carrier directly whether your dog's breed is excluded, and get the answer in writing — this varies more between carriers than almost any other renters coverage detail.


Second, your liability limit. Leases that require insurance most often demand $100,000, but a serious bite claim can exceed that. Raising the limit to $300,000 typically costs only a few dollars a month.


Third, the other half of the risk: liability covers people your dog hurts, not your dog. A separate pet insurance policy is what covers the vet bills when your own dog is the one who gets hurt or sick.


## Common questions


Does renters insurance cover pit bulls?


It depends on the carrier. Some exclude pit bulls and several other breeds from liability coverage entirely; others have no breed list and underwrite the individual dog. If you own a commonly excluded breed, confirm coverage in writing before you buy — and when you compare quotes, make breed acceptance part of the comparison.


What if my dog bites another dog?


Injury to someone else's pet is property damage in insurance terms, and the liability portion of a renters policy generally covers it, along with the owner's related costs.


Does renters insurance cover dog bites away from home?


Yes. Personal liability coverage follows you and your dog — a bite at the park or on a walk is treated the same as one in your apartment.


Does my landlord's insurance cover my dog?


No. Your landlord's policy protects the building and the landlord's own liability. If your dog bites someone, the claim lands on you — which is exactly why many leases now require tenants to carry their own liability coverage.
